model: Bank FCFE (distributable earnings after CET1 retention) at cost of equity (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Reserved 1H2026 profit not in CET1, after the EUR0.40 interim dividend paid 10-Aug-2026
equity_bridge.note: 2Q26 press release: reserved profits not included in CET1 EUR2,725m less interim dividend 0.40 x ~2,858m shares = EUR1,143m. Earmarked for the final 2026 distribution; earned before the forecast window starts.
0.1pp x RWA EUR341,946m; distributable under policy

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Total shareholders' equity CAGR is negative (-1.9% 5yr) while EPS CAGR is +27% and revenue +5.5%: ING has distributed ~100% of earnings plus excess capital (EUR3.1-4.5bn/yr buybacks) since 2021, shrinking equity and share count; the EPS CAGR also starts from the 2020 COVID provisioning trough (EPS 0.64). BVPS CAGR is the meaningful per-share book measure.
historical_growth.notes: Bank: FCF CAGRs not meaningful (OCF dominated by deposit/loan flows). FY2023 step-up is the rate-cycle NII peak (NII 15,976 vs 13,756), FY2024-25 NII normalised lower while fee income grew 8,354 vs 4,805 in FY2022.

scenario_narratives.base: ING delivers its upgraded outlook: total income >EUR24.5bn in 2026 and >EUR26bn in 2027 as NII recovers on replicating-portfolio reinvestment and deposit/lending volume growth (mobile primary customers +377k in 2Q26) while fees compound high single digits toward EUR5.3-5.5bn. Opex held near EUR13bn and risk costs stay ~20-25bp, giving ROTE of ~16% and distributable earnings of ~EUR6.4bn in year one, paid out as ~50% cash dividend plus buybacks at a ~13% CET1. Growth fades to nominal-EUR 2.5% and margins drift back toward through-cycle levels.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fee franchise (investment products, insurance distribution, Wholesale Banking capital-markets) and deposit gathering in Germany/Spain outrun guidance; ECB rates stay ~2% so deposit margins hold while NII rides a growing balance sheet; cost discipline lifts the PBT margin to ~45.5% and ROTE toward 18%, with capital-light growth keeping retention modest.
scenario_narratives.bear: Euro-area recession in 2027 (ING's own IFRS 9 downside scenario): risk costs roughly double to ~45-50bp with Wholesale Banking Stage 3 files and Dutch/German mortgage stress, ECB cuts toward 1% compress replicating-portfolio and savings margins, and income stalls; geopolitical/sanctions and Polish/Turkish tax or FX shocks add leakage. RWA still grows from rating migration, so retention eats a larger share of a smaller profit. ROTE falls to ~11-12% before partial recovery.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ING is valued on what it can distribute: attributable earnings less the CET1 needed to support RWA growth at its ~13% target, discounted at a 9.75% EUR cost of equity. Deposits and wholesale funding are operating liabilities (net_debt = 0); past earnings already reserved for distribution and the small CET1 surplus are added in the bridge. Per-share values are in EUR and converted to USD per ADS (1:1) at the dated EUR/USD rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: risk costs at 2020 levels (EUR2.7bn) would remove ~EUR1.4bn of distributable profit in that year
ECB rate path: deposit/replicating-portfolio margins drive ~65% of income through NII
Cost of equity: each 0.5pp on the 9.75% CoE moves base value roughly 6-7%
Regulatory capital: Basel IV output floor phase-in or a higher Dutch systemic buffer could lift the CET1 target above 13% and cut buybacks
FX: USD value per ADS moves one-for-one with EUR/USD; the rate is pinned at 2026-10-02 and is not refreshed by refresh_price.py
Polish and Turkish subsidiary tax, FX and sovereign risk; Russia exposure run-off

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (ING, NYSE) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range USD 23.64-37.52. INGA.AS and EURUSD=X from the same API for the parity check.
data_sources.financials: ING_Metrics.csv / ING.duckdb (core_metrics + kpis, EUR millions), ING 2Q2026 press release (equity, reserved profit, intangibles, CET1, RWA, share table, buyback, outlook), ING FY2025 Annual Report / 20-F (ETR, buybacks, NCI, SBC note).
data_sources.qualitative: ING 2Q2026 press release outlook for 2026/2027; FY2025 Annual Report outlook and IFRS 9 macroeconomic scenarios. ING_Analysis.json was not yet available at build time.

inputs.sbc_source: ING FY2024/FY2025 20-F: share-based payment arrangements were terminated in 2023; variable pay is cash/deferred cash. SBC = 0 (SBC-zero market, band collapses).
inputs.fx_note: EUR->USD 1.1257, Yahoo EURUSD=X at 2026-10-02T21:29Z. ADR ratio 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share. Parity: INGA.AS EUR 30.685 (2026-10-02 close) x 1.1257 = USD 34.54, within 0.7% of the NYSE close at inputs.price_as_of (gap = Amsterdam 15:38Z close vs NYSE 20:00Z close, intraday FX/equity move). All per-share values computed in EUR and converted at this rate; weighted_iv is USD per ADS.
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,859.7m shares outstanding ex-treasury at 30-Jun-2026 (2Q26 press release share table) less ~22.8m still to be bought under the EUR1.0bn programme announced 30-Apr-2026 (EUR350m done at 30-Jun; remaining EUR650m at ~EUR28.5 avg; ends by 26-Oct-2026). Equity already deducts the full EUR1.0bn commitment, so the share count is aligned to it. No convertible/option dilution (share plans terminated 2023). Held flat thereafter: future buybacks are the FCFE itself and are not double-counted.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in EUR, single rate for all scenarios (risk charged in the flows via the bear case, not stacked into the rate): Dutch 10Y ~2.9% + beta ~1.2 x EUR ERP 5.5% = 9.5%, +0.25pp for Turkey/Poland/emerging and Wholesale Banking exposure = 9.75%. Equals BMO/NAB house bank CoE in their currencies.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: lease costs already inside operating expenses and hence inside pre-tax profit; lease liabilities (EUR1.05bn) are operating funding, not deducted.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI (~EUR275m/yr, mainly ING Bank Slaski and TMB stake) folded into the combined tax+NCI leakage rate (cash_tax_rate_path 32.5%); NCI equity NOT deducted in the bridge. TTM calibration: PBT 9,832 -> attributable net 6,701 = 31.8% leakage.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md (bank row) -> FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, house bank precedent (BMO, NAB.AX, USB). Mapping: revenue = total income; 'EBITDA margin' = profit before tax margin (after risk costs and opex, so D&A = 0 and the D&A line is not used); 'cash tax' = tax + NCI leakage to attributable net result; 'capex' = CET1 retention = 13% target CET1 x RWA growth (RWA0 EUR341.9bn, CET1 capital EUR44.7bn at 30-Jun-2026), expressed as % of the year's income; SBC = 0. Resulting flow = distributable earnings = what ING pays as dividends + buybacks under its ~13% CET1 policy. net_debt = 0: deposits (EUR773bn), debt securities (EUR166bn) and subordinated loans incl. AT1 (EUR19.1bn, classified as liabilities, coupons already in PBT) are operating funding, not net debt. Equity bridge adds the reserved H1-2026 profit not yet distributed and the CET1 surplus over 13%. FY0 is TTM to 2Q2026 on reported figures (resilient net profit equalled reported in 2Q26).

bear.capex_pct_path_rationale: RWA still grows 3% for two years (rating migration in a downturn inflates RWA even as lending stalls), then 2%.

base.growth_rates_rationale: Y1 (Jul-26..Jun-27) blends guidance: 2026 total income >EUR24.5bn (1H26 EUR12.1bn) and 2027 >EUR26bn -> ~EUR25.5bn, +7%. Then fee growth (~8-10%) on a ~2-3% NII base fading to 2.5% nominal EUR growth.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: PBT margin. TTM 41.3%. 2027 guidance: income >26bn, opex ~13bn ex incidentals, risk costs ~EUR1.4-1.6bn (~20-25bp, TTM 1.3bn) -> ~44%; less ~1pp incidental items -> 43.5%. Fades to 42.5% long-run for cost inflation and through-cycle risk costs (2015-25 avg impairments ~6% of income).
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: CET1 retention = 13% x RWA growth of 3.5%/yr (RWA +1.8% YoY at 2Q26; loan growth ~4% partly offset by RWA optimisation) fading to 2.5%, as % of income. Terminal year equals CET1/income (1.78) x g/(1+g), consistent with Gordon growth.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_rationale: Guided ETR 29-31% (higher Polish bank CIT from 2026; 1H26 30.0%) + NCI ~2.5% of PBT = 32.5%.

bull.capex_pct_path_rationale: RWA growth 4.5% fading to 3.0% at 13% CET1.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% house default): a large European universal bank is exposed to a credit cycle the base case does not price, and ING's own IFRS 9 macro view puts 20% on a downside recession and says the balance of risks is negative. Base 50%: management has just upgraded 2026/27 guidance and the 1H26 run-rate supports it. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): the bull needs fee outperformance, stable ECB rates and cost discipline simultaneously, and a 13% CET1 policy leaves little excess capital to surprise with.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
